ads.caption:
Atelier Veyra opens on a single line of type over a cinematic aerial, then descends through ten scenes to street level. The homepage is a camera move rather than a page you scroll.

We build sites this way for practices whose work is visual and whose first impression carries most of the sale.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: Live at growthterminal.io/atelier-veyra. Every frame in the post is the running site.
ads.alt_text: Growth Terminal poster reading: A cinematic homepage for an architecture practice, above a browser window showing an aerial view of a building at golden hour.

ads.caption:
A hospitality site lit like the room it is selling. Warm near black ground, a second warmer surface for panels, and cream rather than white for type.

The accent is brass. It reads as a material the property already contains rather than a colour chosen for a button.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: Proportion is the point. The accent is three percent of the page and appears once per view.
ads.alt_text: Colour specification for luxury hospitality: warm near black ground, cream ink, brass accent, shown as a proportion bar.

ads.caption:
A founder site organised around the work rather than the biography. One page, a fixed navigation rail, and a contact action that stays in view at every scroll position.

We build personal sites for founders and operators whose reputation is the thing being evaluated.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.alt_text: Growth Terminal poster reading: A founder site built around the work, not the biography, above a browser window showing a portfolio site.

ads.caption:
Nexus Workflow is an operations tool. A request arrives, it validates the detail, applies the routing rules, and hands the job to a named person.

The intake screen does the unglamorous part: it checks the fields, normalises the text, and tells you where the request is going before it goes there.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: The interactive version runs entirely in the browser with sample data, so nothing is sent anywhere. These screens show it in our own design system.
ads.alt_text: Growth Terminal poster reading: An operations tool that turns a request into assigned work, above a dark product interface showing a request intake form.

ads.caption:
Architecture sites carry photography that already contains every colour the page needs. So the palette gets out of the way: stone ground, a slightly deeper surface, near black ink.

One earth accent, held for navigation states and the enquiry.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: Sixty percent ground is not emptiness. It is what makes the work look considered.
ads.alt_text: Colour specification for an architecture practice: stone ground, near black ink, terracotta accent, shown as a proportion bar.

ads.caption:
A materials library rendered as a browsable set rather than a specification PDF. Each specimen is its own object, lit consistently, labelled with its finish and treatment.

We build product showcases for businesses whose catalogue is currently a file that gets sent once and opened never.

DM BUILD to talk about yours.
ads.alt_text: Growth Terminal poster reading: A materials library built to be browsed, above a browser window showing a dark materials grid.

ads.caption:
Advisory and legal sites earn trust through restraint. Near white ground, deep ink, and a single restrained blue reserved for the decisions a visitor can actually take.

Colour used sparingly reads as confidence. Colour used everywhere reads as a template.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: The accent appears on one action per screen. Everything else stays neutral.
ads.alt_text: Colour specification for professional services: near white ground, deep ink, restrained blue accent, shown as a proportion bar.

ads.caption:
Three stages of Nexus Workflow run without anyone watching. Intake, validation, routing. The fourth waits for a person, because that is the part that needs judgement.

Every step is written in plain language rather than codes, so an operator can read what happened without learning the system first.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: The interactive version runs entirely in the browser with sample data, so nothing is sent anywhere. These screens show it in our own design system.
ads.alt_text: Growth Terminal poster reading: Three stages ran without a person, the fourth waits for one, above a dark product interface showing a run log.

ads.caption:
We build our own site to the standard we apply to client work. One idea per screen, the interface explaining itself, and nothing on the page that is only there to fill space.

Websites, immersive digital experiences, AI systems, business tools, and the infrastructure connecting them.

Start a project at growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: The clearest way to judge a studio is the work it does when it is its own client.
ads.alt_text: Growth Terminal poster reading: Our own site, built to the standard we apply to client work, above a browser window showing the Growth Terminal homepage.

ads.caption:
Development sites live on daylight photography, so the interface stays bright and steps back. Near white ground, a cool surface for cards, deep ink for type.

One deep accent marks the enquiry, which is the only action on the page that matters.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: Twelve percent ink. Enough for hierarchy, not enough to compete with the renders.
ads.alt_text: Colour specification for real estate development: daylight ground, deep ink, teal accent, shown as a proportion bar.

ads.caption:
Selected Works presents one project per view. The image at full weight, the year, typology and location set beside it rather than beneath it.

For an architecture practice or a developer, the portfolio is the proposal. It is worth designing as carefully as the work it contains.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: Structure, hierarchy and pacing are the design decisions here. The photography is doing less work than it appears to.
ads.alt_text: Growth Terminal poster reading: One project per view, at full weight, above a browser window showing a selected works page.

ads.caption:
Automation is worth having up to the point where judgement starts. After that it should stop and hand over cleanly.

Nexus Workflow hands over with an owner, a state, and an approval that has to happen before anything reaches the client. Automation without that is a faster way to send the wrong thing.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: The interactive version runs entirely in the browser with sample data, so nothing is sent anywhere. These screens show it in our own design system.
ads.alt_text: Growth Terminal poster reading: Automation that stops where judgement starts, above a dark product interface showing a work order handoff.

ads.caption:
Nothing at full strength. A warm off white ground, a soft green surface, and ink that is dark without being black.

The restraint is the product. A wellness site that shouts contradicts the thing it is selling.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: Low saturation across the whole palette, including the accent.
ads.alt_text: Colour specification for wellness and hospitality rooms: off white ground, soft green surface, muted green accent, shown as a proportion bar.

ads.caption:
The studio page carries its argument in typography alone. One weight, one measure, generous line spacing, no imagery above the fold.

Type is the first signal of seriousness a visitor receives and it costs nothing but judgement. We treat it as a primary design decision rather than a default.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.alt_text: Growth Terminal poster reading: Typography that carries the page on its own, above a browser window showing a studio page.

ads.caption:
Dark ground, high contrast type, and a single signal colour that means something. On a product interface the accent is a state rather than decoration.

If it appears more than once in a view it stops being a signal.

→ growthterminal.io
ads.first_comment: Fifty eight percent ground, three percent accent. The ratio is what keeps a dark interface readable.
ads.alt_text: Colour specification for technology and product: dark ground, high contrast ink, blue signal accent, shown as a proportion bar.
